color.$description: Dark theme surfaces, text, state layers and status colours. Adopted from shadcn/ui's default theme on the `zinc` base (its neutral ramp is Tailwind v4's `zinc`, in OKLCH); the status and content-kind hues are Tailwind v4 palette steps. Dark is the default theme. Nothing here is a v1 value — see design/README.md.

bg.$description: zinc-950. shadcn `background`: the window ground behind every panel.

panel.$description: zinc-900. shadcn `sidebar`: chrome surface — sidebar, header, tab bar.

elevated.$description: zinc-800. shadcn `muted`: the inset surface for fields, chips and badges.

raised.$description: zinc-800. shadcn `secondary`: secondary buttons, segmented on-state.

raised-2.$description: zinc-700. Highest neutral surface: scrollbar thumb, switch off-track.

border.$description: shadcn `border` in dark is white at 10%, not a solid grey — it holds its weight over every surface in the ramp instead of only over one. 1.25:1 on --bg: decorative separation only, never the sole boundary of a control (see --border-strong).

border-strong.$description: The boundary of an interactive control — input, checkbox, switch track, segmented button. WCAG 1.4.11 wants 3:1 for a boundary that identifies a component, and shadcn's own --border is 1.25:1. Measured 3.76 on --bg, 3.82 on --card, 3.64 on --elevated. Do not use it for dividers; the visual weight is the point and it is wrong everywhere else.

divider.$description: Hairline between regions. Lighter than --border so a separator never reads as a control edge.

dim.$description: zinc-400. shadcn `muted-foreground`: secondary text. 7.56:1 on --bg, 5.66 on --elevated.

faint.$description: Tertiary text — timestamps, counts, placeholders. Deliberately between zinc-400 and zinc-500 rather than on a scale step: A11Y-10 requires it clear AA because it labels real meta text, and zinc-500 does not on --elevated. 6.13 on --bg, 4.59 on --elevated, 5.26 on --selected.

mute.$description: zinc-500. 4.12:1 on --bg — below AA, deliberately. Decorative only (disabled glyphs, separating dots); A11Y-10: never the sole carrier of text.

hover.$description: Neutral hover state layer. This is shadcn's `accent` — its menu/list hover surface, NOT the brand colour.

accent-hover.$description: Hover fill for a solid --accent button: --accent mixed 12% toward --accent-away, the pole opposite --on-accent, and never toward the surface. Diluting toward the surface moves the fill toward the ink on whichever theme the page is on the ink's side of the fill — that is how shadcn's 10% alpha lands the label at 4.02:1 against a 4.5 floor. Away from the ink it can only rise: 5.77 worst, where the rest state is 4.78. 12% is about one Tailwind palette step. The tradeoff: in dark, the two accents with white ink darken on hover, so the fill falls from 3.12 to 2.35 against --elevated. A filled button is identified by its rest state; the hover state is not its boundary.

selected.$description: Accent-tinted selection fill for list rows and the active nav item. Mixed in oklab so the tint stays perceptually even across all six accents.

selected-edge.$description: The selection marker: a bar or border at full accent strength. Selection CANNOT be carried by --selected alone — the tinted fill differs from --bg by 1.09-1.32:1 across the six accents and from --hover by almost nothing, so a selected row and a hovered row look alike and neither is distinguishable at WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1. Raising the tint far enough to reach 3:1 makes every selected row a coloured block. The edge measures 3.75 worst against --selected and clears 3:1 against --bg by construction (it is the focus-ring colour). Do not use --border here; it is 1.25:1.

alpha-selected.$description: The accent alpha behind --selected, in one place so nothing re-derives it.

err.$description: red-400 — shadcn's `destructive` in dark, verbatim. 6.93 on --bg.

on-err.$description: Foreground on a solid --err fill. Dark ink, not white: shadcn pairs its dark `destructive` (red-400) with white and that measures 2.75:1, which fails A11Y-10 on every destructive button in the app. Dark ink measures 6.25. This is the one place the adopted system is overridden on contrast rather than followed; light keeps white ink because there --err is red-600.

err-hover.$description: Hover fill for a solid --err button. Same construction as --accent-hover, with the pole written out rather than a token because --on-err does not vary by accent: the ink is dark here, so the hover mixes toward white. 6.25 at rest, 7.22 on hover.

ok-strong.$description: AA-corrected foreground variant. In dark the -400 steps already clear AA on their own tints, so these alias the base hue; light is where they differ.

c-text.$description: Content kind: text. zinc-400 — plain text gets the neutral, so a coloured glyph always means something.

c-secret.$description: Content kind: secret. rose-400 — next to --err on purpose: a detected secret is a warning about the item, not a failure.

c-unknown.$description: The kind set is closed and ends in `unknown`, which must never render blank; it falls back to the text-kind colour.

withheld.$description: Fill of the slot where a sensitive item's content would be. INV-10 / CLAUDE.md rule 4: the content is ABSENT — the bridge sends `content: null` — so this must read as an empty slot, not as text behind glass. There is deliberately no blur token; v1's --mask-blur:6px is the treatment the manifest README rules out, and re-adding one would make withheld content look present.

withheld-border.$description: Outline of the withheld slot. It is a real button (A11Y-3), so its boundary carries the 1.4.11 weight.

withheld-fg.$description: The 'Sensitive — activate to reveal' label. 5.32 on --withheld, 6.09 on --selected.
